newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican air crash blamed on human error - report.
newsitem.headline: Dominican air crash blamed on human error - report.

text.p: A plane crash in February off the Dominican Republic that killed 189 people, mostly German tourists, was caused mainly by human error, according to a report by U.S. and Dominican investigators.

In a copy of the report obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, the Dominican office of Civil Aviation and the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board determined that the probable cause of the crash of the Boeing 757 was the crew's "confusion and lack of knowledge" of the aircraft's systems.
The 757 leased to the Dominican national airline Alas Nacionales by Turkish carrier Birgenair plunged into the sea on February 9 shortly after taking off from the Dominican resort of Puerto Plata.
All 189 people on board died in the disaster.
The crash report is scheduled to be released on Friday.

Analysis of contents of the flight data recorder showed that at one point the captain said, "My velocity indicator is not working." The Turkish crew had little training in the 757's systems and instruments, the report said.
Investigators said the crew had been advised by the control tower to verify the operational condition of the motors and the plane's instruments.
The investigation concluded that the aircraft pilot, Ahmet Erdem, 62, could not determine his speed and position as the plane plunged toward the ocean.
The crew also failed to respond quickly to a "stick shaker warning" which caused the steering column to vibrate so that the aircraft stalled and plunged toward the sea, according to the report.
During the plane's last moments, the crew told air traffic controllers, "There is something strange. There are a few problems."
